root_cause.text: The GCS page protection macros (_PAGE_GCS/_PAGE_GCS_RO) unconditionally set the PTE_SHARED bits (bits 8-9), which on systems with FEAT_LPA2 are repurposed as high-order output address bits (bits 50-51), causing corrupted page table entries and translation faults.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states: "When FEAT_LPA2 is enabled, bits 8-9 of the PTE replace the shareability attribute with bits 50-51 of the output address. The _PAGE_GCS{,_RO} definitions include the PTE_SHARED bits as 0b11 ... but using this macro directly leads to the following panic." The patch removes the fixed macros and uses a runtime-variable `gcs_page_prot` that clears `PTE_SHARED` when LPA2 is enabled.
